I still hold it, and it is now better characterised. With audit_max_rounds uncapped, tp audit --status emits max_rounds:null and rounds_remaining:null but OMITS budget_exhausted — three fields from one §10.1 clause, two explicit-null and one vanishing. 0 is the default, so the KeyError case is the default repo, and SKILL.md line 146 lists budget_exhausted among what --status shows. New this round: tp review --status behaves identically, so this is shared v0.35.0 surface and a repair here would move review's payload too — a version's change, not this audit's.

auditRecord now routes through runTPFence with unattended pinned false rather than inheriting os.Environ(). That closes a real fixture-flag hazard, since tp run gives the quality gate TP_UNATTENDED=1, and the comment records the measurement rather than asserting it: four tests in audit_stamping_test.go and audit_nextaction_count_test.go fail under an ambient TP_UNATTENDED=1 when inherited, and pass either way once pinned.

Test 31 was renamed off an uncounted quantifier: it claimed the three fields appear nowhere else while the body checked four outputs, and auditSignalFields has a third call site at run_status.go:147 — now named, with the test that owns that claim. The §6.1 reversal asserts the write RESOLVES to blocking rather than merely exiting 0, and asserts both halves of the invisible premise: the fixture rows carry no severity key, and AuditRowsClean is false over them under blocking.
